source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Verify SUT status after using SF600 flash successfully .

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Verify SUT status after using SF600 flash successfully .

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: SF600 ROT flash tool + signed PFR image (user-provided)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- ROT(PFR) FW Flash (ROT/PFR FW): flash the ROT PFR firmware via the SF600 flash tooling. Agent can verify post-flash SUT status from OS sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -t 2>&1 | tail -n 30; echo "---system status---"; uptime; lspci 2>&1 | wc -l 2>&1"; the ROT PFR flash itself uses the vendor SF600 tool + signed image and is a firmware write.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the post-flash system status (dmesg tail, uptime, device count) so the user confirms the SUT is stable after the ROT(PFR) FW flash succeeded.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: flashing ROT/PFR firmware is destructive; only use the approved SF600 image and never auto-run during production.

original_test_intent: Program the approved ROT/PFR firmware through the SF600 path and verify exact firmware readback plus complete SUT root-of-trust, management, boot, PCIe and host health afterward.
original_method: A qualified operator connects and maps the SF600 fixture to the exact ROT target; after immutable image/tool/compatibility approval, the agent runs the vendor flash once, captures raw output/readback, executes required power/reboot recovery and compares full post-flash health with retained baselines.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must physically attach the SF600 programmer and verify its clip/cable/target orientation. After that setup, the approved flash, readback and health evidence can be automated.
required_inputs: Stable ROT/PFR hardware identity, board/SKU and SF600 target mapping
Current/target versions, signed image hash/signature and compatibility matrix
SF600 tool/version/license, exact invocation, voltage/power sequence and timeout
Known-good recovery image, rollback and OOB/console recovery
safety_requirements: Do not connect or flash an unidentified device and verify programmer voltage/orientation/power state before writes.
Reject unsigned, incompatible or ambiguous images and preserve pre-flash firmware readback where permitted.
Keep power stable except as the validated procedure specifies; stop on disconnect, signature failure, timeout or partial write.
No automatic retry, alternate target guess or unapproved power action.
agent_execution_scope: After operator setup/approval, validate target, tool and image identities and execute the immutable SF600 command once.
Capture raw progress/status, verify target readback/version/integrity and run full BMC/ROT/BIOS/PCIe/host comparisons.
Report the flash/tool result separately from engineer verdict.
engineer_actions: Physically connect and confirm the SF600 target/orientation.
Approve image compatibility, power sequence and recovery.
Review firmware/readback/health evidence and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its post-flash SSH snippet has unsafe nested quotes and only samples dmesg/uptime/device count; it is not the SF600 command or integrity proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not invent SF600 syntax. Use only the owner/vendor validated invocation and image, then perform exact firmware readback and comprehensive health comparison.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: SF600 flash and post-flash SUT-status requirement plus 5/20-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: AWAIT VALIDATED SF600 PACKAGE; RETAIN PHYSICAL FIXTURE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind target identity, programmer mapping, tool hash/version and signed image to an approved manifest; perform one write with raw log, independent readback/hash or vendor verify, then staged recovery/health checks.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact ROT/PFR device, board/SKU, SF600 programmer and image.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SF600 hardware/tool, ROT/PFR image, board, BIOS and BMC versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner/vendor SF600 connection, programming, compatibility and PFR recovery procedures.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target/image provenance and integrity/readback evidence without replacing SF600.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No loss; physical programming and post-flash health remain required.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target, image, tool, sequence, verify and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Post-boot health alone cannot prove the correct root-of-trust image was programmed.

project_override_considerations: Projects select target image/version and recovery path. Missing package/spec data makes execution not ready, not permanent BLOCKED; a different programmer or in-band updater changes the tested method and needs explicit approval.
expected_evidence: ROT/SKU/programmer target map, versions, signed image/tool hashes, compatibility/recovery and authorization
Physical connection/orientation record and pre-flash identity/readback
Exact SF600 command/raw output, verify/readback and power/reboot timestamps
Post-flash ROT/PFR/BMC/BIOS/PCIe/host/SEL health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires status verification after successful SF600 flash; omitted technical parameters are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: V3.1 does not treat absent image/tool/project parameters as permanent BLOCKED. The execution remains NOT READY until supplied, and the manual fixture makes it PARTIAL.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keep PARTIAL but reject its incomplete/broken post-check as full coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain all firmware safety gates but change BLOCKED to readiness-not-ready under locked V3.1.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates physical fixture setup, automated write/tool result and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Requires exact target/image provenance and verified firmware readback rather than inferring success from a short post-boot health sample.
independent_technical_reasoning: SF600 requires physical programmer attachment, so the case is PARTIAL. Once that setup and validated package are supplied, the flash and evidence are automatable; missing firmware inputs affect readiness rather than creating permanent blockage.
